Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the rear-end collision you
were involved in at an intersection in Sugar Land, Texas. Can you confirm you're comfortable continuing?
A: Yes, that's fine.
Q: Please describe in your own words what happened leading up to the collision.
A: I was stopped at a red light in the right lane. I had come to a full stop and was waiting for the signal to change. The
vehicle behind me didn't seem to slow down in time.
Q: How fast do you believe the other vehicle was traveling when it made contact?
A: It wasn't going very fast, maybe a little faster than a crawl. But I didn't have time to react, and I felt the impact pretty
hard through my seat.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt at the time?
A: Yes, I was.
Q: Did you notice any injuries immediately after the collision?
A: Not right away. I got out and walked around a bit, but later that evening my right shoulder started to ache and then
got worse. Litfing my arm above my head is painful now.
Q: Have you sought medical treatment for the shoulder?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the following morning. They took X-rays and told me to follow up with an
orthopedic specialist.
Q: Do you have any prior injuries or conditions affecting that same shoulder?
A: I had some soreness a few years ago from a sports injury, but it had resolved and I hadn't had any problems since.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about the collision or your injuries?
A: Only that I'm still having trouble sleeping on that side and I've had to take time off work. I'd like to be made whole
for what I've gone through.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
A: Thank you.
</page>
